svg.text: The pipeline map: from a pull request to the VPS and the Pi
Concept 3 (also Concepts 4, 6, and 9) · the assembly line .github/workflows/ci.yml: six stations (jobs) · red = the next stations are skipped
the robot only checks: no secrets, no pushing, no deploying
The branch rule = a barrier in front of main (Concept 11)
lifted only when three required checks are green: verify, test, build
the Merge pull request button is locked,
= a push to main, on to band 2
Merge = a push to main: the robot runs again; a new release reaches the VPS (pushed) and the Pi (pulls by itself)
2 · Every push to main (= a pull request that was merged)
secrets and write permissions exist only here
the same as in the pull request,
is set: SSH with the robot
the Pi asks by itself "a new release tag?",
knock on a Pi behind the home router
a push without a new version (for
no images); staging, the tag, and
the deploy skipped; a skipped job
The robot's token permissions per job (Concept 6): the default for every job contents: read (only reads the repo's content) · build + packages: write
staging + packages: read · tag-release contents: write (the only one that writes to the repo) · deploy-vps without a token: permissions: {}
Example: the author's simulated robot (ci.yml as is, Raspberry Pi 5 arm64, local images and registry; the Indonesian edition's lab, not GitHub)
verify ±110–135 seconds ∥ test ±75–105 seconds → build ±95–125 seconds → staging ±50–75 seconds → tag-release ±3–5 seconds → deploy-vps ±30 seconds
merge → the simulated VPS deployed in ±5–6½ minutes (a lab example, not GitHub)
a release whose staging is red (a broker mistyped on purpose) never gets a tag: the simulated VPS and Pi stay on the old version
on GitHub, staging also pulls ±1.1 GB of images (TimescaleDB, Grafana, Mosquitto + the new images): its time not measured by the author
